source: The descriptions of the installed skills that compete with this plugin's for the same requests, copied from each plugin's skills/<id>/SKILL.md: Google Workspace, Slack, GitHub, Linear, Jira, Granola, Wispr Flow, Metaview, Plaud, Tavily and History.

skills.metaview: Load before the first Metaview tool call (metaview_*, tools.metaview.*). For the user's recruiting interviews and candidates in Metaview - "what did <candidate> say about X", "summarise yesterday's screen with <name>", "which interviews did <interviewer> run last week", a candidate's interviews, including requests to guess a candidate's age, family or other personal traits, interview counts and themes by role, profiles and scorecards, reports, sourcing, screening, sequences and job posts, and Metaview sign-in. Not for non-hiring meetings (Granola), calendar scheduling or Slack.
skills.metaview-candidate-brief: Prep me for my interview with a candidate, brief me before a round, build a debrief or evidence pack, compare candidates or finalists for a role, check a scorecard against the transcript, or draft my interview feedback or scorecard, from Metaview. Builds a sourced brief and leaves every hiring decision to the user. Load with metaview before the first Metaview tool call. Not for non-hiring meetings or calls (granola-meeting-brief).
skills.metaview-write: Load before any Metaview change - regenerating notes or adding note sources, saving or sharing a snippet or clip, creating a report, AI field or note template, sourcing searches and candidate feedback, posting candidates to an ATS, application review rejects or progress and ICP changes, screening plans or invitations, sequences and outreach, contact enrichment, job posts - or before reporting a Metaview bug or problem to Metaview.
skills.granola: Load before the first Granola tool call (granola_*, tools.granola.*). For questions about the user's Granola meetings: what was said, decided or assigned, notes, transcripts, follow-ups, questions across meetings, saving meetings as Markdown, or Granola sign-in and sign-out.
skills.granola-meeting-brief: Prep me for my next or tomorrow's meeting, brief me before my call with a person or company, catch me up on a project, or recap a period's meetings, from the user's Granola notes. Builds a sourced brief of decisions, open questions and who owes what. Load before the first Granola tool call.
skills.wisprflow: Load before the first Wispr Flow tool call (wisprflow_*, tools.wisprflow.*). Use when the user names Wispr Flow, Flow or its Notetaker or Scratchpad, or gives a notes.wisprflow.ai link - their recorded meetings (what was said, decided or assigned, transcripts, Flow Summaries, attendees, folders), Scratchpad notes, the calendar Wispr Flow holds, or Wispr Flow sign-in. Also when the user asks Wispr Flow for dictation history, the dictionary, snippets or usage, or to transcribe an audio file, which this connection can't do. Not for Granola or Plaud, or for transcribing audio without Wispr Flow named.
skills.wisprflow-meeting-brief: Load before the first Wispr Flow tool call for a brief, when the user names Wispr Flow, Flow or its Notetaker, gives a notes.wisprflow.ai link, or chooses Wispr Flow as the source - prep for their next or today's meeting from Wispr Flow's calendar, upcoming events and pre-reads, a catch-up on a recurring meeting before a call with a person or company, or a recap of a period's Wispr Flow meetings. Builds a sourced brief of decisions, open questions and who owes what. Not for Granola notes.
skills.opencode-gws: Use for any request about the user's Gmail, Google Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Tasks or other Google Workspace data, such as "check my inbox", "what's on my calendar", "find that doc", "send this email" or "share the file": how the gws_* tools find, read and change it (accounts, plan then approved commit, paging, errors). Use it instead of any gws-* CLI skill or a gws shell command, which skip the plugin's approvals.
skills.opencode-gws-recipes: Load before the first gws_read or gws_plan for an everyday Google Workspace task; it has the ready request: unread or recent mail and who sent it, mail in a time window, replies and drafts, the next meetings or a week's schedule, finding, summarising, sharing or trashing Drive files and Google Docs, reading or appending Sheets rows, and the standup, meeting-prep and weekly-digest reports. Prefer it to any gws-* CLI skill.
skills.slack-search: Use when the user wants to find, read, summarise or cite anything in their Slack (messages, threads, channels, people, canvases, lists or files), asks what was said or decided in Slack, wants to post, reply, draft or schedule a Slack message, or wants a script or cron job that reads Slack. Covers Slack's own tools in OpenCode, private-content consent, permalinks, and scripts through OpenCode's tools RPC instead of a Slack token or the Web API.
skills.linear: Read before your first Linear tool call, linear_issues included. Use whenever the user asks about Linear or their Linear work - my issues, what I'm working on, what's in this cycle, a project's progress, an issue's comments, counts by state, a teammate's assignments - or names an identifier such as ENG-123 or a linear.app link. Covers choosing between linear_issues and list_issues, filters, paging, counts and citing links. Not for GitHub or Jira issues.
skills.jira: Load before the first Jira tool call (jira_*, tools.jira.*). For the user's Jira work items (tickets, issues, epics), a key such as PROJ-42 or an atlassian.net link, JQL search, comments, logged time, boards, sprints, the backlog, story points, versions, filters and dashboards, and Jira sign-in or site selection. Not for Linear issues, GitHub issues, or meetings and transcripts. Confluence pages are outside this Jira-only plugin and it requests no Confluence access, so say that once rather than searching another app for them.
skills.jira-write: Load before any Jira change - creating or editing a work item, transitioning status, commenting, logging time, linking items, converting a work item to a sub-task, attaching a file, watching, moving a sprint or releasing a version, or creating a board - and before explaining why a delete or a project setting is unavailable.
skills.github-pr-review: Review or summarise a GitHub pull request from its description, changed files, diff, earlier reviews and CI checks, and find out why CI failed, now or on an earlier run, without changing anything unless asked. Use when the user asks to review, summarise or check a GitHub pull request (a URL, OWNER/REPO#123 or a number), or why its CI or a check failed.
skills.opencode-plaud: Plaud voice recordings in OpenCode, to list, search and read recordings made with a Plaud device or app, with their transcripts, notes and highlights. Use when the user mentions Plaud, a voice recording or voice note, or something they recorded, such as "what did I record this week?" or "the action items from my last recording".
skills.tavily: Search the web and read web pages with Tavily - current facts, news, documentation, finding the right page on a site, mapping or crawling a site, and gathering cited sources. Use when the answer is on the web, when a page is one that webfetch cannot read, when checking whether Tavily is set up, or when writing a script or cron job that searches the web without a model (Tavily's tools RPC, no API key in the script). Not for the project's files or the user's own tools.
skills.history-recall: Look things up in the user's past OpenCode (coding-agent) sessions with the history tools, and cite them as (ses_… #seq). Use it for "how did we fix…", "what did we decide about…", "like last time", "what did I work on yesterday / this week", "which sessions changed <file>", "why is <file> like this", "what did that session do", or what OpenCode sessions cost per day, week or project. Load it before the first history tool call. Not for meetings, chat threads or saved memory notes, and not a stand-in for git history when the user asks about sessions.
